cards.text: Mary and Joseph's baby Boy is eight days old, so it's time for His circumcision. It's also time for His name: Jesus. My name got CARVED into my handle, friend, so believe me, I know naming day is a big deal.

cards.question: Mary and Joseph came up with the name Jesus on their own.

cards.text: Then the time of purification under the Law of Moses is complete. So His parents pack up the baby and hit the road to present Him to the Lord.

cards.question: Mary and Joseph bring baby Jesus to ___ to present Him to the Lord.

cards.text: Why the trip? It's written right there in the Law of the Lord, and it's about baby boys like Jesus.

cards.question: The Law of the Lord says every ___ male shall be consecrated to the Lord.
The Law of the Lord also specifies a sacrifice for this visit. What is it?

answers.text: A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons
A young bull or two spotless goats
A spotless heifer or a young ox

cards.text: Now meet Simeon, a righteous and devout man in Jerusalem, with the Holy Spirit upon him, waiting for the consolation of Israel. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer waiting for somebody to open it, so believe me, I RESPECT a man who waits.

cards.question: The Holy Spirit has revealed something to Simeon about his waiting. What is it?

answers.text: He won't see death before seeing the Lord's Christ
He'll serve as high priest before he dies
He'll see the temple rebuilt in his lifetime

cards.text: Now watch the timing on this, baker. Mary and Joseph carry baby Jesus into the temple courts to do what was customary under the Law, and Simeon is right there.

cards.question: Simeon ends up in the temple courts that day just by chance.

cards.text: Simeon takes the baby in his arms and blesses God. Somebody hands ME a baby, all I've got is a mustache, and I'm holding that child like a HOT cookie tray, sweating the whole time.
Then Simeon says, "Sovereign Lord, as You have promised, You now dismiss Your servant in peace."

cards.question: Simeon tells God He can now dismiss His servant in peace. Why can Simeon say that?

answers.text: His eyes have seen God's salvation
His years of temple work are done
His family is finally safe at home

cards.text: Simeon says God has prepared this salvation in the sight of all people. Not a few folks peeking in. ALL people.

cards.question: Simeon calls God's salvation a light for revelation to the ___ and glory to God's people Israel.

cards.text: Mary and Joseph are amazed at what's been said about their Child. Me, I'd be standing there with my eyebrows shot up PAST my chef's hat.
Then Simeon blesses them and turns to Mary. He's got more to say about this Child.

cards.question: Simeon tells Mary what her Child is appointed to cause in Israel. What is it?

answers.text: The rise and fall of many
A new king for every tribe

cards.question: Simeon tells Mary that everyone in Israel will speak well of her Child.

cards.text: Right, this Child will be a sign that will be spoken against. And Simeon says it all has a purpose: what's hidden inside people is coming out into the open.

cards.question: Simeon says that through this Child, the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed.

cards.text: Then Simeon has a word for Mary herself: a sword will pierce her soul as well.
Now meet Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher. She's well along in years, and she had been married for seven years.

cards.question: After those seven years of marriage, Anna was a widow to the age of ___.
Where does Anna the prophetess spend her days as a widow?

answers.text: She travels from town to town
She stays at home in Asher

cards.text: Anna worships night and day, fasting and praying. Night AND day, friend, and I can't stay awake through a twelve-minute oven timer.
Then Anna comes forward at that very moment. Talk about TIMING.

cards.question: When Anna comes forward at that moment, what does she do first?

answers.text: She asks Simeon for a blessing
She brings a gift for the Child

cards.question: Anna speaks about the Child to all who were waiting for the ___ of Jerusalem.

cards.text: Mary and Joseph do everything the Law of the Lord requires. Then it's time to head home.

cards.question: Their business at the temple is done. Where do Mary and Joseph take Jesus home to?

cards.text: And the Child grows and becomes strong. Same tiny baby Simeon held in his arms, baker. Growing strong.

cards.question: As Jesus grows, He is filled with wisdom, and the grace of God is upon Him.

findings.problem: Discovery questions dominate the walkthrough rather than remaining a few exceptions. For example, the name's origin (stop 1 card 2), the sacrifice (stop 1 card 7), Simeon's revelation (stop 1 card 9), what the Child is appointed to cause (stop 2 card 3), Anna's whereabouts (stop 2 card 10), the family's destination (stop 2 card 16), and Jesus' wisdom and grace (stop 2 card 18) all require new information that cannot be worked out from the earlier cards. Together with the other unsupported choices, this leaves most choices dependent on discovery or luck rather than reasoning.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The setup says only that the Law concerns baby boys like Jesus. It gives no basis for reasoning out "firstborn" rather than "youngest" or "royal," so the blank asks for unseen Law wording instead of an inferable meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card says that what is hidden inside people will come out into the open, directly supplying the answer to card 6's question about whether the thoughts of many hearts will be revealed.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Knowing only that Anna was well along in years gives the baker no way to reason out exactly eighty-four rather than sixty-two or ninety-nine. The blank asks for an unseen number and can only be answered by luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: "And the Child grows and becomes strong.", "Same tiny baby Simeon held in his arms, baker.", and "Growing strong."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
